title: Drifting a vehicle
summary: Drifting in R.E.P.O. is a system of its own: it starts from a speed and an angle, pushes and turns the vehicle, ramps the speed up, changes the drag on the way out, lights the wheels and rumbles the pad, and pays a boost when you exit at speed.
body: A vehicle does not slide by accident. Drifting is a system the body can be given, with its own switch, which is why a car can be built to drift and another can be built not to.

A drift starts under conditions. There is a threshold for how fast you have to be going and a threshold for the angle, and once a drift begins it lasts at least a minimum time rather than flickering on and off.
It pushes and it turns. A drift applies a force, adds a yaw boost and redirects some of the velocity, which is why the vehicle both slides and swings round rather than only travelling sideways.

It has its own turning and its own speed bounds. Drift turning speed, a maximum drift speed and a minimum ratio of speed all apply while the drift is running, so the handling while sliding is configured separately from the handling while gripping.
Going into a drift ramps up. The speed is raised over a set ramp time rather than being switched instantly, which is why the slide builds instead of snapping into place.
Coming out of it changes the drag. There is a drift drag and a default drag, with a smoothing time between them, so the vehicle settles back into grip rather than losing the slide all at once.
Low speed is handled apart. There is a separate low-speed drag with its own easing duration and a starting multiplier, which is why a slow drift does not feel like a fast one.

The drift is lit and drawn. There are drifting particles with a transform of their own, and a drift light with settings that differ by drift level, so the effect changes as the drift gets harder rather than staying one colour.
It has a loop of its own. The drift sound loop runs between a lowest and a highest pitch, which is why the noise rises with the slide instead of repeating flatly.
Staying fast rewards it. There are separate boost times for full speed and for low speed, a threshold for what counts as full speed, and rates for how the boost grows over time and at hyper speed.

The drift is drawn at more than one strength. There are drifting particles for three levels, with a particle set aside for the moment the first boost level is reached, so a light slide and a hard one do not throw the same effect.

The vehicle is configured around the drift as well. The boost has a forward push and a speed multiplier of its own, and the body carries a force multiplier, an extra turn angle you may take by hand and the colliders it is made of.

It is felt as well as seen. There are rumble strengths for position and rotation, a rumble speed and a multiplier when the boost is active, so a drift reaches the controller rather than only the screen.
What this entry does not tell you: how fast you must be going to drift, how long a boost lasts, or how much speed a drift adds. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Drifting is a system with its own switch on the vehicle.
A drift starts from a speed threshold and an angle threshold, and lasts at least a minimum time.
It applies a force, a yaw boost and a redirect multiplier.
It has its own turning speed and speed bounds.
The speed ramps up over a time when a drift starts.
Leaving a drift applies an exit boost and switches between a drift drag, a default drag and a smoothing time.
At low speed a separate drag, easing duration and starting multiplier apply.
Drifting has particles with a transform, and a light with settings per drift level.
facts.evidence: identifiers: driftingParticlesTransform, driftParticles, driftLight, driftLightSettings, driftLevelSettings

facts.claim: The drift loop runs between a lowest and a highest pitch.
Full and low speed each have a boost time, with a threshold for full speed and rates for growing the boost over time and at hyper speed.
facts.evidence: identifiers: driftBoostTimeAtFullSpeed, driftBoostTimeAtLowSpeed, driftBoostFullSpeedThreshold, driftBoostSpeedOverTimeRate, driftBoostHyperSpeedRate

facts.claim: The drift carries rumble strengths for position and rotation, a rumble speed and a boost multiplier.
The drift is drawn in levels: there are drifting particles for three levels and a particle for the moment the first boost level is reached.
The boost has a forward push and a speed multiplier of its own, and the vehicle records a force multiplier, an extra turn angle it may take by hand and its own colliders.
facts.evidence: identifiers: driftBoostLevel2ForwardBoost, driftBoostLevel2SpeedBoostMultiplier, forceMultiplier, manualTurnExtraAngle, vehicleColliders
